verdicts.reason: The evidence names only Banque de France (French state body), which runs the national component, and the Eurosystem, which operates the T2S platform and counts as EU; nothing shows any non-EU operator, host or data access, so 'mixed' is not supported, and the shared platforms depend on the Eurosystem.
The Senate report says the DGA (French Ministry of the Armed Forces) awarded Artemis to Atos-Bull, Capgemini and Thales-Sopra Steria, all headquartered in France, with no non-EU party mentioned.

The Senate report says only that DGSI 'acquired the service offered by' Palantir (US), not that Palantir hosts, operates or can access the data; the second part of the holding, DRSD's SIRCID, is described in the same report as a national solution contracted to Airbus Defence & Space, so the evidence does not establish a category for the holding.
CASD is a French public-interest group (State via INSEE, GENES, CNRS, Ecole polytechnique, HEC Paris, Banque de France) that designed its own dedicated secure equipment, and no foreign party appears.
VaS data is stored on tape run by INA and on Nubo, the State's sovereign cloud run by DGFiP (both French state bodies), with no foreign host shown.
